chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad who said:

I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three (things) are from the practices (sunnah) of the Messengers: perfume, the removal of (unwanted) hair, and frequency of marital relations.'

key_terms.أَخْذُ الشَّعْرِ: The removal or trimming of hair; refers to grooming practices such as removing unwanted body hair
key_terms.الطَّرُوقَةِ: Marital relations; from the root meaning 'to come at night,' indicating intimate relations with one's wife
key_terms.الْعِطْرُ: Perfume or fragrance; using pleasant scent is a recommended prophetic practice
key_terms.سُنَنِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ: The collective prophetic practices — sunnahs attributed not to one prophet alone but to all the Messengers as a shared tradition

ai.seo_question: What are the three practices of the Prophets mentioned by Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies three practices as being part of the collective sunnah of the Prophets and Messengers: the use of fragrance, the grooming of hair (particularly removal of unwanted hair), and maintaining frequent marital relations. This hadith reflects the Islamic tradition that the Prophets modeled ideal human conduct across all aspects of life, including personal hygiene and family life. The audience of the eighth Imam's companions would have understood these as recommended (mustahabb) acts with prophetic sanction, not mere cultural preferences.
